idiom_name: struct graph plus one sqlite3 transaction, FK ON DELETE CASCADE
implementation_notes: C has no object-relational mapper, so the composite is a struct that owns its dependent structs and the mapper functions are hand-written around the sqlite3 C API. Persist the whole graph inside one BEGIN/COMMIT pair and declare the child table with a FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE CASCADE so a dependent that leaves the cluster also leaves the store; note that SQLite enforces foreign keys only after PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON on each connection, and that constraint checks can be deferred to commit time when the save order is awkward.
pitfalls: PRAGMA foreign_keys is off by default and is set per connection: a mapper that opens a second connection silently writes orphan rows unless every open helper enables it.

Without an explicit BEGIN ... COMMIT the autocommit default executes each statement independently, so a failure halfway through leaves a half-saved cluster even though the function reads as one operation.
The root key must be read back (sqlite3_last_insert_rowid) before dependent rows can reference it, and a deferred FK only moves the failure to COMMIT, it does not remove it.
